text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Outspoken business executive and Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries president, Jonee Blanchfield, is embroiled in a controversy involving her family company which sources say has over the years supplied jewellery and cosmetics to retailer Truworths, a public company of which Blanchfield is group managing director.

- Zimbabwe's Criminal Investigation Department is understood to have raided over the past 30 days the offices of at least 40 safari operators and seized documents relating to their operations. This follows allegations that the major players in the industry, mostly whites, are externalising their earnings.
- A businessman in Zimbabwe's second city of Bulawayo has entered into a joint venture project leading Australian investors to build houses for the middle-income bracket starting next January.

- Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe on Thursday said the southern African country saw some of its fastest economic growth ever in 1996, with all sectors except for mining doing well to push gross domestic product up eight percent.
